title: Meeting preview shows the day before the date you picked
why: The date input holds the right value. The shift only appears when a date-only string is formatted in a time zone west of UTC.
finding: `parseDateInput('2026-10-20')` is `new Date(value)`, which means UTC midnight. Formatted in `America/New_York` that is 8 PM on Oct 19, so the preview read ‘lunes, 19 de octubre’ for a meeting on the 20th.
actual: The preview line reads "Reunión el lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026 a las 09:30" — one day earlier than the selected date 2026-10-20 — and the same one-day shift appears for every date entered (the prefilled 2026-10-19 rendered as "Reunión el domingo, 18 de octubre de 2026 a las 10:00"). The date input and time select correctly hold 2026-10-20 and 09:30, but the preview shows the previous calendar day.
expected: With the date field set to 2026-10-20 and time 09:30, the live preview line under the form should read "Reunión el martes, 20 de octubre de 2026 a las 09:30" — the same calendar date (Tuesday, October 20, 2026) that the user selected in the date input, so the form gives feedback matching the chosen schedule.

reproduce.text: Type a title for the new meeting into the meeting title field
Set the meeting date to a near-future date
Pick a start time from the time dropdown
Pick a duration from the duration dropdown
Before submitting, read the live 'Meeting on …' summary line shown under the form

rootCause.text: In src/lib/dates.js, parseDateInput(value) returns `new Date(value)`. For the date-only string '2026-10-20', `new Date('2026-10-20')` constructs a Date at UTC midnight (2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z). Schedule.jsx line 77 (describe = (dateStr) => formatLongDate(parseDateInput(dateStr), language, timeZone)) then passes that instant to formatLongDate, which formats it with Intl.DateTimeFormat in the workspace timeZone 'America/New_York' (UTC-4 in October). At 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z it is 20:00 on 2026-10-19 in New York, so the preview renders 'lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026' — one day earlier than the selected date. The date-only input value must be parsed as a local (or UTC-timezone) date rather than left at UTC midnight when formatted in a non-UTC timezone.

rootCauseSteps.text: SearchSources 'parseDateInput' shows the function defined in src/lib/dates.js line 14 as `return new Date(value)` and that Schedule.jsx line 77 formats it via describe = (dateStr) => formatLongDate(parseDateInput(dateStr), language, timeZone), i.e. the preview's date goes through the UTC-midnight parse and the timezone-aware formatter.

Evaluating new Date('2026-10-20') in the workspace timezone proves the shift: the string parses to ISO 2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z and Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone 'America/New_York' formats that instant as 'lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026'.

The visible state after the time selection confirms the defect: the date input holds '2026-10-20', the time select holds '09:30', and the rendered [data-testid=schedule-preview] element contains 'Reunión el lunes, 19 de octubre de 2026 a las 09:30' — the one-day-earlier date.
